decisions.reason: As the publicly announced flagship with heavy sunk costs and centrality to the firm's stated direction, management remains strongly committed and will persist rather than withdraw.
The dedicated page and multiple models reflect substantial visible investment and sunk development costs, making withdrawal unlikely despite reduced website presence.

Although only a website mention, the crate line involves significant engineering resources and fits the core returnable packaging portfolio, so escalation leads management to continue and justify the investment.
The pallet line has sunk development costs and aligns with the firm's logistics focus, and withdrawal would mean admitting failure of resources already committed, so the firm persists.
Its own page shows public commitment, but as a single product it carries less sunk investment than the lines, so while escalation favors persistence, the probability of withdrawal is slightly higher.
